note: The instruction regression corpus. Every sentence a user might type at the task box,
and what the tier ladder must do with it.
`expect` is one of tier0 | escalate | refuse. `reason` is the *recorded* reason, and
asserting it is the point: a sentence that escalates for the wrong reason is a passing
test hiding a broken rule. Two of the entries below are transcripts of real runs on
w3schools.com/howto/howto_css_contact_form.asp in which the agent did the opposite of
what it was told and then reported success.
`refuse` means Tier 0 will not attempt a partial parse at all -- currently only
negation. It still escalates; the difference from `escalate` is that no amount of
looking at the page could change the answer.
No values in here that are not obviously synthetic. This file is read in the open.
Read by extension/src/worker/instructions.test.ts, which is a fast unit suite:
parseGoal and chooseTier are both node-pure, so none of this needs a browser.

cases.goal: Dont fill last name with Leo
cases.why: Run on the w3schools contact form. It filled Last Name with Leo. The verb pattern is anchored at the end and not at the start, so `fill` matched inside the sentence and the four characters that reverse it were never looked at.

cases.goal: Fill last name with leo and subject as Write Something
cases.why: The original M16 failure, and it now parses whole. The second clause has no verb, but it opens with a field name the table knows -- see labelledPair -- so 'subject as Write Something' reads as putting that text in Subject, which is what it means. M16's acceptance was 'fills both fields or escalates the whole goal, never one field and done'; filling both is the better half of that.

cases.goal: do not fill the email
don't submit the form
fill first name with leo but not the last name
never click submit
fill the form without the email
fill everything except the email
cases.why: Scoping this correctly is the reasoning a planner is for. The grammar refuses rather than implementing scope.

cases.goal: fill first name with leo unless it is already set
avoid the subject field
skip the phone number
fill last name with leo instead of the first name
click save rather than submit
this isn't the right form
fill last nmae with leo
cases.why: The grammar reads it -- coverage is 1 -- and the resolver then cannot find a field called `last nmae`. Escalating on resolution rather than on comprehension is the honest reason for a misspelling, and it is the one Tier 1 can actually answer.

cases.goal: tpye my emial
cases.why: No verb the grammar knows, so nothing parsed at all. That is the same shape as a real open-ended task and is filed as one.

cases.goal: enter Asha Menon as full name
cases.why: `as` puts the value first here. Only one of the two readings names a field the alias table knows, so there is nothing ambiguous about it.

cases.goal: subject as Write Something
cases.why: A field name and a value with no verb between them, which is the commonest shorthand anybody types. Read after every pattern has declined, so an explicit verb always wins.

cases.goal: enter subject as message
cases.why: Both readings name a field the table knows. No regex can tell which was meant, and choosing one silently is what a sixth pattern would do.

cases.goal: fill first name with leo
fill first name with leo and fill last name with menon
cases.why: Every clause parses, so every clause is acted on and the completion check has two intents to verify.

cases.goal: fill first name with leo, fill last name with menon, then click submit
fill first name with leo and book an appointment
cases.why: One clause parsed and one did not. The whole goal escalates -- executing the half that parsed would split one instruction across two tiers and leave the page in a state neither planned for.

cases.goal: book the next available appointment
finish this form
can you please fill first name with leo now
cases.why: Politeness is consumed by an explicit ignore list, so coverage reaches 1 without the residue rule being lowered to a threshold.

cases.goal: please fill last name with menon
fill subject with please click submit
cases.why: The value is data. `please` inside it is not filler to be stripped and `click submit` is not a second instruction -- there is no separator, so there is no second clause.

cases.goal: fill message with call me now
cases.why: A message box has no class, so trailing politeness is left alone. Stripping `now` here would be a value silently truncated, which the agent would then go and type.

cases.goal: click submit
type leo in the first name box please
fill the form, where first name is dilip, full name is dilip reddymalla
cases.why: fill the form is a preamble (ignored); where is leading filler; clauses parse as labelled pairs.
